title: Basis of the Rise in the Full-Term Risk Premium for Insured-Requested Coverage Increases — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
**Rise in the full-term risk premium — coverage increases the insured requests (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own), tiers without ICC coverage, no loan transaction)**

The rise rule:

1. When the request carries no full-term risk premium from the rating engine, there is no rise.
2. Otherwise, when a re-rate credit from an applied Elevation Certificate was booked on the current term after the request was recorded, the rise is the request's full-term risk premium less the risk premium booked for the term at its start, because both figures stand on the rating basis the request was rated on.
3. Otherwise the rise is the request's full-term risk premium less the rated risk premium on the policy.

The first line that holds decides. The risk premium booked for the term at its start is the risk premium charged for the current term at new business or at renewal. A re-rate credit counts only when it is a credit on the risk premium line from an applied certificate, posted on the current term after the date the request was recorded.

| Request carries an engine figure | Re-rate credit after the request | Rise |
|---|---|---|
| No | Either | None |
| Yes | Yes | Request figure less the risk premium booked at the term start |
| Yes | No | Request figure less the rated risk premium on the policy |

*Hypothetical illustration.* A request figure of 2,000.00 dollars, a rated risk premium on the policy of 1,600.00 and a risk premium booked at the term start of 1,800.00: the rise is 400.00 without a later re-rate credit and 200.00 with one.
